To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the optimal diagonal loading is inversely proportional to the number of snapshots and (b) the MSE of both estimators is dominated by the squared bias, which is inversely proportional with the number of snapshots.

the optimal diagonal loading is inversely proportional to the number of snapshots, that the optimal diagonal loadings are different for the two power estimator and that the one with the lower optimal diagonal loading outperforms the one with the higher one.

the optimal diagonal loading for the MPDR-based spatial power estimations is a function of the number of snapshots, the number of sensors as well as the number of sources, that for a fixed number of snapshots, as the number of sensors and/or the number of sources increase, the optimal diagonal loading decreases and the optimal diagonal loading is the same for the two MPDR-based power estimators when the number of snapshots is large.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the optimal diagonal loading for two diagonally loaded minimum power distortionless (MPDR) response-based spatial power estimator in the snapshot deficient regimes.
two MPDR-based spatial power estimator and the optimal diagonal loading for them in the snapshot deficient scenario.
the analysis of the performance of two MPDR-based spatial power estimator in the snapshot deficient environment and it provides a guideline for the optimal diagonal-loading design.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the power estimator based on the MPDR beamformer is the preferred choice for snapshot deficient data.
the optimal diagonal loading for the two power estimator is different.
the diagonal loading that minimally increases the squared bias, while keeping the variance as small as possible, would be a good candidate for the optimal diagonal load.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the optimal diagonal loading for the MPDR-based spatial power estimations is a function of the snapshot ratio, and that it is not the same for all power estimators.
the proposed optimal diagonal loading for the MPDR-based spatial power estimations is not only a function of the number of snapshots but also a function of the spatial correlation matrix.

in the snapshot deficient sample regime, the performance of the power estimator based on the diagonal loaded sample correlation matrix is significantly better than that based on the diagonalized sample correlation matrix.
The main takeaway from our work is that
in order to minimize the estimation MSE of MPDR-based spatial power estimations, one must use the optimal diagonal loading which is different for the two estimators.
the optimal diagonal loading is inversely proportional to the number of snapshots used in the estimation of the spatial correlation matrix.

the optimal diagonal loading for the two power estimator depends on the number of snapshots, the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), the spatial signature of the signal, and the spatial signature of interfering noise sources.
